Exercise 1. (A) Download the appropriate libraries and packages (Hint: take special notice of the file extension for the NC Counties data (Hint: use load())). (B) Using the Covid April 14 and the NC Counties data, make a map of the cumulative number of confirmed cases, per capita, in each county in North Carolina. (3 points)

library(tidyverse)

Exercise 2. (A) Download the Covid Data 1. (B) Combine the Covid Data 1 to the data frame that you created in Exercise 1. Next, create a variable that represents the number of confirmed cases that occurred from April 13 and April 14. Lastly, compute the confirmed per capita cases and visualize it in a map. (3 points)
#(A)
covid_april_13 <- read_csv("covid_hopkins_04-13-2021.csv")

── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Delimiter: ","
chr  (4): Admin2, Province_State, Country_Region, Combined_Key
dbl  (9): FIPS, Lat, Long_, Confirmed, Deaths, Recovered, Active, Incident_R...
dttm (1): Last_Update

ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.

#(B)
covid_geom <- covid_geom %>%
  left_join(covid_april_13, by=c("GEOID" = "FIPS")) %>%
  mutate(apr14diff = Confirmed.x - Confirmed.y,
         apr14_percap = apr14diff/estimate)


ggplot(data = covid_geom) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = covid_geom$apr14_percap))

Exercise 3. (A) Utilize the Covid April 14 and US data sets, make a map of the cumulative number of confirmed cases per capita, in each state in the United States. (2 points)
load("us_geom.RData")



covid_state <- covid_april_14 %>%
  group_by(Province_State) %>%
  summarize(total = sum(Confirmed))



covid_us_geom <- us_geom %>%
  mutate(GEOID = as.numeric(GEOID)) %>%  
  left_join(covid_state, by=c("NAME" = "Province_State")) %>%
  mutate(state_percap = total / estimate)


ggplot(data = covid_us_geom) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = covid_us_geom$state_percap))
Warning: Use of `covid_us_geom$state_percap` is discouraged.
ℹ Use `state_percap` instead.
